# QS-CFW-5010-61 - Quality specification - axle hub CFW-5010-61 (4140) Rev A

## Scope
This quality specification applies to finished axle hub CFW-5010-61 forgings produced at Plant P3 for part CFW-5010-61. It defines acceptance criteria for hardness, bore dimensional tolerance, and forging weight, and documents inspection methods, rationale for acceptance criteria, examples of acceptable and nonconforming conditions, and required records. This document is intended for use by production, heat treatment, quality assurance, and shipping.

## Requirements

| Parameter | Requirement | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Material/part | CFW-5010-61 (4140) | Part identification must match supplied order |
| Hardness (after final process) | 22-28 HRC. | Hardness across critical surfaces must be within range |
| Bore diameter tolerance | ±0.10 mm. | Measured at specified bore feature for fit accuracy |
| Maximum forging weight | 5.4 kg. | Includes any machining stock retained for finish operations |

Background and rationale:
- Hardness range 22-28 HRC. is specified to ensure required combination of wear resistance and toughness for axle application while remaining compatible with downstream machining operations.
- Bore diameter tolerance ±0.10 mm. is specified to control press-fit/interference characteristics with mating shafts and to ensure consistent assembly performance.
- Maximum forging weight 5.4 kg. limits material handling risk and ensures compatibility with established tooling and heat treatment fixtures.

## Inspection method

General statements:
- Inspection is performed by Quality Assurance personnel following established receiving and in-process inspection workflows. Measurements are recorded to permit traceability to production lot and furnace/heat batch identifiers.
- Inspectors shall confirm part identification marking or packaging to match the production order before dimensional or hardness checks.

Hardness inspection:
- Hardness readings shall be taken on representative features and potential critical faces identified on the engineering print. Indent locations shall be on clean, flat surfaces free of scale, heavy oxide, or painted surfaces that could affect reading quality.
- For parts exhibiting a hardness outside 22-28 HRC., additional measurements surrounding the initial indication are recommended to determine if the condition is localized or systemic.
- Instrument calibration status shall be verified prior to use. Calibration records for hardness testing equipment must be maintained.

Dimensional inspection (bore):
- Bore diameter shall be checked using an appropriate bore measuring instrument consistent with the feature geometry. The measured value must fall within ±0.10 mm. of the nominal bore callout on the drawing.
- For features that will be machined after forging, inspectors shall verify that the measured bore leaves sufficient machining allowance compatible with downstream operations. If doubt exists regarding allowance, consult process engineering.

Weight verification:
- Forging weight shall be verified against shop traveler or casting/forging ticket. The final forging must not exceed 5.4 kg. for handling and tooling compatibility.
- If a part exceeds 5.4 kg., stop production of that lot and initiate nonconformance handling per this document.

Examples:
- Example acceptable condition: hardness readings of 24 HRC. and 26 HRC. on opposing faces, bore measured within ±0.10 mm. of nominal, and forging weight recorded as less than or equal to 5.4 kg.
- Example nonconforming condition: single reading of 20 HRC. on a critical face, bore out of tolerance beyond ±0.10 mm., or forging weight greater than 5.4 kg.

Records to keep:
- Hardness test reports showing location, readings, tester ID, and calibration status.
- Dimensional inspection reports showing measured values for the bore feature, inspector ID, and instrument used.
- Forging weight records tied to lot/heat numbers and the shop traveler.
- Nonconformance reports and disposition records when applicable.
All records shall be retained in the document control system and made available for internal review and customer audits.

## Nonconformance handling

Identification and segregation:
- Any part or lot found to be outside the requirements in the Requirements table must be immediately identified and segregated from conforming material. A visible tag indicating quarantine status is recommended to prevent inadvertent use.

Notification and containment:
- Quality shall notify production and process engineering of nonconforming findings promptly. Production of similar parts should be halted until containment and root cause are assessed.

Disposition:
- Disposition options include rework, repair, use-as-is with concession, or scrap. The selected disposition must be documented and approved by authorized personnel.
- For hardness values outside 22-28 HRC., disposition must consider potential impacts on mechanical performance. Options may include reheat/tempering if process capability and material condition permit, or rejection if material integrity is suspect.
- For bore dimensions outside ±0.10 mm., options may include corrective machining where drawing tolerances and material condition allow, or rejection if the bore cannot be brought into tolerance without violating design requirements.
- For forgings exceeding 5.4 kg., the lot must be evaluated for tooling and handling implications. Unless approved disposition exists, excess-weight forgings shall be rejected.

Root cause and corrective action:
- A root cause investigation should document process step(s) leading to nonconformance, corrective actions taken to prevent recurrence, and verification of effectiveness.
- Corrective actions may include changes to forging charge, trim parameters, heat treatment procedures, or tooling maintenance, as applicable.

Final disposition and release:
- Only authorized personnel shall sign off on final disposition. Released parts must have all inspection records and dispositions attached to the lot's quality file prior to shipment.

Audit and review:
- Nonconformance trends shall be periodically reviewed by quality leadership to identify systemic issues. Corrective measures shall be implemented where trends indicate repeat occurrences.

Appendix (records examples):
- Typical record set for a conforming lot: hardness test report, dimensional inspection report with bore readings, forging weight ticket, and inspection release sign-off.
- Typical record set for a nonconforming lot: all of the above plus quarantine tag, nonconformance report, root cause analysis, corrective action documentation, and final disposition approval.

End of document.
